title: The `testing` package: your first test, `t.Run` and subtests

videos.script: Until now you checked a program by running it and reading what it printed. That works once, while you watch. A test checks itself, every time, on any machine. {{package}} The last six lessons of the course grow one small package that counts the words in a text. It starts with one function. {{first}} Then the first test. It feeds the function a sentence anybody can count by eye. And it fails. The function looked finished, and it was counting full stops as part of the words. {{fix}} You fix the code, not the test, and run it again. {{subtests}} Next, subtests. One test grows into five named cases: capitals, accents, an empty text. One of them fails, and the failure turns out to be a question about what a word is. {{helpers}} Last, helpers that report the right line, and a temporary directory that cleans up after itself. {{close}} Lesson 26 turns those five cases into a table.
